learn.text: Small games mean lots of touches. Play a quick pass, then shift into a new space and ask for the ball again straight away. Never hide. The more touches you get, the faster you improve, which is why Shankly filled training with little games.

facts.text: As a player, Shankly won the FA Cup with Preston North End in 1938 and also played for Scotland.
In 1972 he put up the famous 'This Is Anfield' sign in the players' tunnel to make visiting teams nervous.

Matt Busby.why: Matt Busby believed in young players and gave them a chance to shine early. His Manchester United teams played bold, attacking football with skilful forwards. He searched for talented teenagers, coached them with care and trusted them in big games. He also pushed for his club to take part in the new European competitions. His kind but firm leadership built a family feeling at the club that lasted for generations.

learn.text: Be brave on the ball. If you have space in front, run at the defender instead of always passing backwards. Try a feint or a sudden change of speed to get past. Busby wanted his young forwards to entertain the crowd and take players on.

facts.text: As a player, Busby won the FA Cup with Manchester City in 1934 and later also played for Liverpool.
He was knighted in 1968 after the European Cup win, and his United sides also won five league championships.

Brian Clough.why: Brian Clough liked football played on the grass, not kicked high into the air. His teams passed the ball along the ground with neat, simple moves. Every player knew their job, and he explained it in just a few words. He believed a smaller club could beat anyone with the right spirit, and his teams proved it. Before coaching, he was a goal-scoring striker for Middlesbrough and Sunderland.

learn.text: Keep your passes low and along the ground. Lock your ankle, use the inside of your foot and push the ball firmly to your partner's feet. A rolling pass is much easier to control than a bouncing one. Clough wanted his players to keep it on the grass.

facts.text: In 1977-78, the very season after winning promotion, Nottingham Forest won the league title under Clough.
His Forest team went 42 league matches in a row without defeat, until Liverpool ended the run in December 1978.

Arsène Wenger.why: Arsène Wenger brought new ideas to English football. He changed what his Arsenal players ate, promoting pasta and boiled chicken over junk food, and used sports science to keep them fresh. His teams played fast, one-touch passing football that zipped from defence to attack. He had a gift for spotting young talent and helping it grow. People nicknamed him 'The Professor' because of his thoughtful, studious style.

learn.text: Try passing first time. As the ball rolls towards you, look up early, pick your target and strike it with one touch. Quick one-touch passes move the ball faster than any defender can run. Wenger's Arsenal used them to slice through teams.

facts.text: In his first season at Monaco, 1987-88, Wenger won the French league title.
In 1998 he became the first foreign manager to win the Premier League and FA Cup double in England.

Valeriy Lobanovskyi.why: Valeriy Lobanovskyi treated football like a science. He studied matches using data and gave every player a clear set of tasks, both with and without the ball. His Dynamo Kyiv teams pressed together, squeezing the space so opponents had no time to think. Players had to be very fit and well organised. He had been a clever left winger, and as a coach he shaped some of the finest Soviet and Ukrainian sides.

learn.text: When the other team has the ball, press as a group, not on your own. The nearest player rushes the ball while the next ones block the passing lanes. If one of you chases alone, it's easy to pass around you. Lobanovskyi's players always hunted together.

facts.text: As a left winger for Dynamo Kyiv, Lobanovskyi was known for scoring goals straight from corner kicks.
As coach, he led Dynamo Kyiv to eight Soviet league titles, and the club later renamed its stadium after him.

Béla Guttmann.why: Béla Guttmann loved attacking football and helped spread the 4-2-4 shape, with four forwards ready to pounce. He travelled the world as a coach, gathering ideas in many countries and sharing them. He had a sharp eye for young talent and gave big chances to rising stars. His Benfica side scored freely and beat Europe's best. Before all that, he was a skilful player in Hungary.

learn.text: Be brave and attack the goal. When you get the ball near the box, take a touch forward and get your shot away before a defender can block it. Aim low and away from the keeper. Guttmann's teams always hungered for one more goal.

facts.text: Guttmann's Benfica beat Barcelona 3-2 in the 1961 European Cup final, then came back from behind to beat Real Madrid 5-3 in 1962.
As a player, he won Hungarian league titles with MTK in 1920 and 1921 and played six times for Hungary.

Vittorio Pozzo.why: Vittorio Pozzo was a careful planner who prepared his Italy teams in great detail. He set them up in the metodo, a 2-3-2-3 shape with a strong centre-half guiding play. He demanded discipline and fitness, and asked every player to put the team first. As a young man he studied and played football in England, then brought those lessons home to Italy.

learn.text: Great teams are built on good basics. Practise a little every day: toe taps, sole rolls and touches with both feet. Do each move slowly and correctly first, then speed up. Pozzo's sides won because they prepared carefully, long before the big matches.

facts.text: Before coaching Italy, Pozzo helped found Torino and played for the club for five seasons.
Under Pozzo, Italy won the Central European International Cup in 1930 and kept the title in 1935.

Mário Zagallo.why: Mário Zagallo was a small left winger who worked very hard in defence as well as attack. That two-way running helped Brazil stay balanced, and he carried the idea into coaching. His 1970 side was packed with star forwards, yet he found a way for them all to play together. Nicknamed the 'Old Wolf', he served Brazil for decades as a player, coach and assistant.

learn.text: Wingers can defend too. When your team loses the ball, don't stop and wait up front. Turn and sprint back towards your own goal, getting between the ball and the net. Zagallo did this as a winger, and it kept his team strong.

facts.text: Zagallo was assistant coach and coordinator when Brazil won the 1994 World Cup.
He coached Brazil to the 1997 Copa America title, beating hosts Bolivia 3-1 in the final.

Telê Santana.why: Telê Santana believed football should be beautiful as well as winning. His teams played short, quick passes and encouraged players to dribble past opponents. Lots of players joined each attack, including defenders and midfielders. His Brazil team of 1982 is still remembered as one of the most exciting ever. Having been a winger for Fluminense, he knew the joy of attacking.

learn.text: Keep the ball close as you dribble, using small touches. Look up to spot the next open space, then burst into it. Use both feet. Santana wanted his players to enjoy the ball and take people on, so practise until dribbling feels fun and natural.

facts.text: In 1971, Santana led Atletico Mineiro to the club's first Brazilian national championship.
He coached Brazil at two World Cups, in 1982 and again in 1986.

Jupp Heynckes.why: Jupp Heynckes built teams that were dangerous in attack and well organised in defence. Even his biggest stars were asked to run, press and help their teammates. He was a calm, respected leader who spoke to players with patience. Before coaching he was a deadly striker for Borussia Mönchengladbach, so he understood what forwards need. His best sides shared both the ball and the hard work.

learn.text: Be unselfish near the goal. In a two-against-one, dribble towards the defender to pull them in. When they come to you, slide a pass sideways to your free teammate for an easy finish. Heynckes wanted his stars to work for each other like this.

facts.text: As a player, Heynckes was part of the West Germany squads that won Euro 1972 and the 1974 World Cup.
In his first spell as Bayern Munich coach, he won back-to-back Bundesliga titles in 1988-89 and 1989-90.

Alf Ramsey.why: Alf Ramsey built teams around hard work and togetherness. His England side often played without old-style wingers, so the midfielders had to run up and down the flanks. Every player knew his job, and nobody mattered more than the team. A former England right-back, he understood defending well. He was quiet and serious, and he planned every detail before a match.

learn.text: Work as a pair in midfield. If your partner goes to press the ball, drop a few steps behind them to cover. If they get beaten, you are ready to stop the attacker. Ramsey's busy midfielders shared their jobs like this all game long.

facts.text: As a player, Ramsey was a right-back who won the league with Tottenham in 1950-51 and captained England three times.
His Ipswich won the Second Division in 1960-61, then became champions of England in their first ever top-flight season.

Pia Sundhage.why: Pia Sundhage wants her players to be brave and confident on the ball. Her teams try to keep possession and build attacks with calm passes. She is known for a warm, cheerful style that helps squads feel like a family. As a player she was a top Swedish striker. She has coached national teams on several continents, spreading her love of the game wherever she goes.

learn.text: Be confident when the ball comes to you. Before it arrives, glance over your shoulder. Open your body so you can see the field, then take your first touch forward and turn. A brave first touch helps your team keep the ball, just as Sundhage asks.

facts.text: As a player, Sundhage won the first women's European Championship with Sweden in 1984 and was the tournament's top scorer.
She was named FIFA World Coach of the Year for 2012, the year she led the USA to Olympic gold.

Jill Ellis.why: Jill Ellis planned carefully for big tournaments and used her whole squad, so fresh legs were always ready. Her USA teams attacked with energy, and her full-backs pushed high to join the forwards. She trusted many different players to step up when it mattered most. Before leading the national team she coached UCLA for years, so she knew how to help young players grow.

learn.text: Defenders can attack too. When your team has the ball on your side, overlap the winger by running past on the outside. Get close to the end line and send a low cross into the box. Ellis's full-backs made runs like this to add an extra attacker.

facts.text: Ellis led UCLA to eight NCAA Women's College Cups, including seven in a row from 2003 to 2009.
She won FIFA's women's coach award for both 2015 and 2019, the first USA coach to win it twice.

Silvia Neid.why: Silvia Neid's Germany teams were tight, tough and organised. Players defended close together and fought hard for every loose ball. She asked her squad to win their one-on-one battles all over the pitch. A skilful midfielder, she had played more than a hundred games for Germany, so she knew what it took to win tournaments. She guided her country through more than a decade of success.

learn.text: Win your battles for the ball. Keep your body between the opponent and the ball, stay low and strong, and keep your touches small. Protect it like treasure. Neid's players were tough to knock off the ball because they shielded it like this.

facts.text: Neid was named FIFA's World Coach of the Year for women's football three times, in 2010, 2013 and 2016.
On her Germany debut in 1982, Neid scored twice, the first just one minute after coming onto the pitch.

Luis Enrique.why: Luis Enrique was a hard-working player who could play almost anywhere, from full-back to forward. As a coach he wants his teams to press high and win the ball back fast, then attack with lots of quick passes. He asks every player, even the forwards, to run and defend for the team. Kids can copy his energy; when your team loses the ball, the first few seconds are the best time to win it back.

learn.text: Luis Enrique teams hunt the ball together the moment they lose it. Practise a quick reaction: the second the ball is lost, sprint at the player who has it, stay on your feet and try to steal it back before they can look up.

facts.text: As a player, Luis Enrique won Olympic gold with Spain in 1992 and played for his country at three World Cups.
As a coach he won the Champions League twice: with Barcelona in 2015, as part of a treble in his first season, and with Paris Saint-Germain in 2025.

Mikel Arteta.why: Mikel Arteta was a calm, clever midfielder who kept the ball moving with short, accurate passes. As a coach he plans every detail, teaching his players exactly where to stand so there is always a pass on. His teams keep their shape, defend as a group and attack with lots of players. Kids can copy his idea that football is a team puzzle; if everyone finds a good space, passing becomes easy.

learn.text: Arteta likes his players to make triangles so the player on the ball always has two passes. Practise with two friends: pass and move, and keep adjusting so the three of you always make a triangle shape.

facts.text: Arteta began his senior career at Barcelona, then won the Scottish league with Rangers and was twice named Everton Player of the Season. He won two FA Cups as an Arsenal player.
After working as an assistant to Pep Guardiola at Manchester City, he became Arsenal manager in 2019. He won the FA Cup in his first season and, in 2026, the Premier League.

Hansi Flick.why: Hansi Flick was a midfielder at Bayern Munich who later spent years learning as an assistant coach before taking charge himself. His teams play with a high line, press as a group and attack quickly and directly when they win the ball. He is known for being calm and friendly with his players, so they play with confidence. Kids can copy his message; be brave, push up together and look forward as soon as you get the ball.

learn.text: Flick teams attack fast after winning the ball. Practise a quick break: when you win it, look forward first, pass or run into space, and try to finish the move before the defenders can get back.

facts.text: From 2006 to 2014 Flick was assistant coach of the Germany national team under Joachim Löw, and helped them win the 2014 World Cup.
He took over Bayern Munich in November 2019, and that season they won the Bundesliga, the German Cup and the Champions League.

Carlo Ancelotti.why: Carlo Ancelotti is famous for his calm way of managing great players. Instead of forcing one system on everyone, he looks at the players he has and builds the team around their strengths. He keeps the dressing room happy and lets his stars play with freedom. Kids can learn from his calm; in a big game, a relaxed mind helps you make better choices with the ball.

learn.text: Ancelotti teams stay calm on the ball under pressure. Practise in a rondo: when the two defenders rush you, keep your head up, take one easy touch and play the simple pass instead of panicking.

facts.text: Ancelotti has won the Champions League five times as a coach, a record. He is the only coach to win league titles in all five of Europe's top leagues.
As a midfielder he won the European Cup twice with AC Milan, in 1989 and 1990. He is one of very few people to win it as a player and as a coach.

Jürgen Klopp.why: Jürgen Klopp became famous for "heavy metal" football: teams that press with huge energy and attack at full speed. He hugs his players, celebrates wildly and makes every game feel exciting. His teams win the ball high up the pitch and attack before the opponents are ready. Kids can copy his spirit; work hard for each other, chase together and enjoy every game.

learn.text: Klopp teams press in pairs so nobody is left alone. Practise with a partner: one of you presses the player with the ball while the other covers behind, then swap jobs as soon as the ball moves.

facts.text: Klopp spent most of his playing career at Mainz, moving from striker to defender. He became Mainz manager when he stopped playing in 2001 and won promotion to the Bundesliga in 2004.
He led Borussia Dortmund to two Bundesliga titles, then won the Champions League with Liverpool in 2019 and the Premier League in 2020.

Zinedine Zidane (coach).why: Zinedine Zidane was one of the most elegant players ever, with amazing control and vision. As a coach he kept things simple and calm, trusting his players and helping them believe in themselves. His Real Madrid teams were brilliant in big knockout games and seemed to grow stronger under pressure. In a tense moment, kids can do what he did and take a breath, trust your skills and play.

learn.text: Zidane loved to control the ball and turn away from pressure. Practise receiving with a light touch, then using the inside or outside of your foot to turn and face forward before a defender can close you down.

facts.text: After coaching Real Madrid Castilla, Zidane took charge of Real Madrid in 2016 and became the first coach to win the Champions League three times in a row.
As a player he won the 1998 Ballon d'Or and was named FIFA World Player of the Year three times, in 1998, 2000 and 2003.

José Mourinho.why: José Mourinho is one of the most successful coaches in football history. He studies every opponent in detail and prepares a plan to stop their best players. His teams are hard to beat: they defend well together and strike quickly on the counter-attack. Kids can learn from his preparation; think before the game about what the other team likes to do, and plan how to stop it.

learn.text: Mourinho teams are very good at getting back into shape. Practise recovering: when the attack passes you, sprint back towards your own goal and get between the ball and the goal before you try to tackle.

facts.text: Mourinho stopped playing young and became an interpreter for coach Bobby Robson at Sporting CP, then worked as his assistant at Porto and Barcelona.
He has won league titles in four countries and won the Champions League with Porto in 2004 and Inter Milan in 2010. He is the only coach to have won all three current UEFA club competitions.

Diego Simeone.why: Diego Simeone, nicknamed "Cholo", was a tough, determined midfielder, and he coaches the same way. His teams defend as a tight, organised unit and fight for every ball. When they win it back, they look to counter-attack fast. He shows how a team that works hard together can beat teams with more famous players. Kids can copy his never-give-up attitude and his love of defending as a group.

learn.text: Simeone teams never give the attacker an easy run. Practise staying low and side-on, showing the attacker towards the touchline, and staying patient until you can win the ball cleanly.

facts.text: Simeone has been head coach of Atlético Madrid since 2011. With them he has won La Liga twice, in 2014 and 2021, and the Europa League twice.
As a midfielder he won more than 100 caps for Argentina, played at three World Cups and won the Copa América in 1991 and 1993.

Vincent Kompany (coach).why: Vincent Kompany was a strong, calm centre-back and a natural leader who captained Manchester City and Belgium. As a coach he wants his teams to be brave on the ball, keep possession and attack with lots of players. He talks to his players clearly and gives them confidence. Kids can learn from his leadership; talk to your teammates, encourage them and keep calm when things go wrong.

learn.text: Kompany likes defenders who are calm with the ball at their feet. Practise building out from the back: receive from your keeper, look up, and pass into a teammate in space instead of kicking it long.

facts.text: Kompany spent eleven years at Manchester City, eight of them as captain, and won the Premier League four times there.
As a coach he won the Championship with Burnley in his first season, then won the Bundesliga in his first season at Bayern Munich in 2025.

Thomas Tuchel.why: Thomas Tuchel is a thoughtful coach who loves tactics and changes his team's shape to fit each opponent. His teams try to keep the ball, press as a group and defend with lots of organisation. He studies the game in great detail and explains clearly to players what he wants. Kids can learn from his curiosity; ask questions, watch games and think about why things work.

learn.text: Tuchel teams look for the side of the pitch with the most space. Practise switching play: if one side is crowded, keep the ball moving and pass to the other side, where there is more room to attack.

facts.text: Tuchel's playing career ended early, and in 2000 he began coaching youth teams at VfB Stuttgart. Later he won the German Cup with Borussia Dortmund and two French titles with Paris Saint-Germain.
He took over Chelsea in 2021 and won the Champions League in his first season. That year he was named The Best FIFA Football Coach.

Lionel Scaloni.why: Lionel Scaloni was a hard-working right-back and right midfielder who played for many years in Spain and Italy. As Argentina coach he built a close, united team around Lionel Messi, where every player works for the others. His sides are well organised, defend together and stay calm in big tournaments. Kids can learn from his idea of a team; when everyone helps each other, the whole team gets better.

learn.text: Scaloni's Argentina loved quick little passing combinations. Practise the give-and-go: pass to a teammate, run straight past the defender, and get the ball back in the space behind them.

facts.text: Under Scaloni, Argentina won the 2022 World Cup and the Copa América in 2021 and 2024.
As a player he won La Liga with Deportivo de La Coruña in 2000. Earlier he won the 1997 FIFA World Youth Championship with Argentina's under-20 team.

Xabi Alonso.why: Xabi Alonso was a deep-lying midfielder famous for his long, accurate passes and powerful shots from distance. He could switch play from one side of the pitch to the other with one kick. As a coach he builds teams that keep the ball, move it quickly and attack with wing-backs high up the pitch. Kids can copy his vision; before the ball arrives, look around so you already know where your best pass is.

learn.text: Alonso always knew where his teammates were before he got the ball. Practise checking over your shoulder: take a quick look both ways before each pass reaches you, so you can play the ball forward with your first or second touch.

facts.text: As a player he won the Champions League with Liverpool in 2005, scoring in the final, and again with Real Madrid in 2014. With Spain he won the 2010 World Cup and two European Championships.
As Bayer Leverkusen coach he won the club's first-ever Bundesliga title in 2024, going the whole league season unbeaten and adding the German Cup.

Enzo Maresca.why: Enzo Maresca was a skilful midfielder who played in England, Italy, Spain and Greece. As a coach he likes his teams to keep the ball and build attacks patiently from the back, with defenders stepping into midfield to create an extra passing option. He learned a lot working with youth players and as an assistant coach. Kids can learn from his patience; you do not have to rush forward, keep the ball until a good chance opens up.

learn.text: Maresca teams love keeping the ball. In a rondo, move to make yourself available, use one or two touches, and keep the ball moving until the defender is tired out.

facts.text: Maresca began his career at West Bromwich Albion in 1998. Later he won Serie A with Juventus and the UEFA Cup twice with Sevilla.
As a coach he won the Championship with Leicester City in 2024. With Chelsea he won the Conference League and the first expanded FIFA Club World Cup in 2025.

Unai Emery.why: Unai Emery is famous for how carefully he prepares. He studies videos of every opponent and gives his players detailed plans for each game. His teams are organised, work very hard and are especially strong in European cup competitions. He started coaching small clubs in Spain and worked his way up. Kids can learn from his hard work; practise the details, and the big moments get easier.

learn.text: Emery teams defend as a group so nobody is left alone. Work with a partner, where one presses the player with the ball while the other stays a few steps behind to cover, and swap jobs whenever the ball moves.

facts.text: As of November 2026, Emery holds the record for the most Europa League titles, with five: three with Sevilla, one with Villarreal and one with Aston Villa.
His coaching career began at Lorca Deportiva, who won promotion in his first season. He then led Almería into La Liga for the first time in their history.

Andoni Iraola.why: Andoni Iraola was a tough, hard-working right-back who was also a good passer. As a coach he is known for teams that press high with huge energy, run hard and attack quickly and directly. His players chase as a pack and try to win the ball near the opponents' goal. Kids can copy his energy, because when your team presses together, even a smaller team can make life hard for big opponents.

learn.text: Iraola teams switch from standing still to sprinting in a flash. Practise your reactions: jog, then explode into a quick sprint on a signal, and stop under control just as fast.

facts.text: Iraola spent almost all of his playing career at Athletic Bilbao, playing 510 competitive matches for the club over 12 seasons, mostly at right-back.
He won the Cypriot Super Cup with AEK Larnaca and promotion with Rayo Vallecano. In 2025-26 he led Bournemouth to the highest league finish in their history.

Cristian Chivu.why: Cristian Chivu was a smart, left-footed defender who could play at centre-back or left-back. He was a leader who captained Ajax as a young player. He was calm on the ball, good at passing and brave in tackles. After his playing days he coached Inter Milan's youth teams before moving up. Kids can learn from his calm defending; watch the ball, keep your position and pass it out cleanly when you win it.

learn.text: Chivu could start attacks from the back with his left foot. Practise passing out of defence: when the ball comes to you, take a touch away from pressure and pass firmly along the ground to a teammate.

facts.text: Chivu captained Ajax before moving to Roma and then Inter Milan. He won the treble with Inter in 2010: Serie A, the Italian Cup and the Champions League.
He played 75 times for Romania. As Inter head coach he won Serie A and the Italian Cup in the 2025-26 season.

Luciano Spalletti.why: Luciano Spalletti is a creative coach known for clever tactical ideas. His teams pass the ball quickly, move into space and attack with lots of players. He likes players who can play in more than one position, so the team can change shape during a game. He has coached in Italy and Russia. Kids can learn from his creativity; try new positions and new ideas, because that is how you learn the game.

learn.text: Spalletti teams pass and move all the time. Practise keep-away: after every pass, move into a new space so the passer always has another option, and keep the ball as long as you can.

facts.text: Spalletti won two Italian Cups in a row with Roma and two Russian league titles with Zenit Saint Petersburg.
He led Napoli to the Serie A title in the 2022-23 season and was named Serie A Coach of the Season.

Massimiliano Allegri.why: Massimiliano Allegri was a midfielder who became one of the most successful coaches in Italy. He believes in keeping football simple: defend well, stay organised and take your chances. He changes his tactics to suit his players and the opponent. His teams are hard to break down and good at winning close games. Kids can learn from his simple ideas; do the basics really well, and good results follow.

learn.text: Allegri teams defend as a solid group. Practise getting goal-side: when an attacker gets past, run back on the inside, between the ball and your goal, before you try to win it back.

facts.text: While playing for Livorno he was nicknamed "Acciughina", which means "Little Anchovy", because he was thin and quick.
Allegri won Serie A with AC Milan in 2011. At Juventus he won five Serie A titles in a row, from 2015 to 2019.

Rúben Amorim.why: Rúben Amorim was a hard-working midfielder for Benfica and Portugal. As a coach he became known for a back three, with wing-backs who run up and down the sides and two attacking players who drift into the spaces between the lines. His teams press as a group and attack with confidence. Kids can learn from his idea of width; if the wide players stretch the pitch, there is more room in the middle.

learn.text: Amorim uses wing-backs who get forward down the sides. Practise overlapping: run down the wing past your teammate, receive the pass in space, and cross the ball low across the goal for a runner.

facts.text: As a midfielder Amorim won three Portuguese league titles with Benfica and played for Portugal at two World Cups.
After winning the League Cup in his half-season at Braga, he joined Sporting CP in 2020 and won the Portuguese league with them in 2021 and 2024.

Michael Carrick.why: Michael Carrick was a calm, deep-lying midfielder whose game was built on passing. He rarely lost the ball, read the play early and kept his team ticking with simple, accurate passes. He was so reliable that coaches sometimes used him as an emergency centre-back. He later became a coach. Kids can copy his calm habits, so look before you receive, keep it simple and make the pass your teammate can use.

learn.text: Carrick's passing was clean and accurate every time. Practise passing through small gates with a partner: use the inside of your foot, keep the ball on the ground and pass it firmly to their stronger foot.

facts.text: Carrick came through West Ham United's youth team and won the FA Youth Cup in 1999 before becoming a first-team player there.
He spent twelve years playing for Manchester United, captaining them in his final season. He won five Premier League titles and the 2008 Champions League there.

Sarina Wiegman.why: Sarina Wiegman was a midfielder and defender who played more than a hundred times for the Netherlands, while also working as a PE teacher. As a coach she is calm, clear and very well organised. Her teams know their jobs, stay together under pressure and keep believing until the final whistle. Kids can learn from her clear thinking; a calm head and a simple plan help a team play its best in big games.

learn.text: Wiegman's teams stay calm and keep their shape. Practise in a small-sided game: after every pass, find a space so your teammate always has a pass on, and talk to each other the whole time.

facts.text: Wiegman won the Women's Euro with the Netherlands in 2017 and with England in 2022 and 2025. She was the first manager to reach five major international tournament finals in a row.
In 1989 she studied at the University of North Carolina in the United States and played for its women's team, which won the national college championship that year.

Emma Hayes.why: Emma Hayes built one of the most successful teams in women's club football at Chelsea. She is known for careful planning, strong team spirit and changing tactics to fit each opponent. Her teams are hard-working, brave and dangerous when they attack. She talks a lot about players growing as people as well as footballers. Kids can learn from her belief that a happy, united team can achieve big things.

learn.text: Hayes' teams attack with purpose and many players join in. Practise in an end-zone game: when your team wins the ball, look for a forward pass or run into space so the team can reach the end zone quickly.

facts.text: Hayes managed Chelsea Women from 2012 to 2024 and won seven Women's Super League titles, including five in a row from 2020 to 2024.
In 2024 she led the United States to Olympic gold at the Paris Games, and she won the first Women's Johan Cruyff Trophy as the best coach in the women's game.

Pere Romeu.why: Pere Romeu was a defensive midfielder as a youngster, but he found his love of coaching early. He worked his way up through youth teams, analysing games and helping players learn. His Barcelona Femení teams keep the ball, pass quickly and press hard to win it back. He is known for his strong relationships with players. Kids can learn from his path; you can learn a lot about football by watching closely and asking questions.

learn.text: Romeu's Barcelona move the ball fast to escape pressure. Try it in a rondo and play one or two touches, pass to the player furthest from the defenders and keep moving into new spaces.

facts.text: Romeu joined Barcelona's La Masia academy as a youth coach in 2017. He later helped coach a group of young players that included Gavi.
He was an assistant to Jonatan Giráldez at Barcelona Femení, then became head coach in 2024 and won Liga F, the Copa de la Reina and the Spanish Super Cup in his first season.

Jonatan Giráldez.why: Jonatan Giráldez started out in youth football and in sports analytics, studying the game in detail. As Barcelona Femení head coach he built a team that kept the ball, pressed hard and won almost everything. He wants his players to be brave, creative and always available for a pass. Kids can learn from his love of study; watching and thinking about football can make you a better player.

learn.text: Giráldez teams always offer the player on the ball several options. Practise making angles: after you pass, move so you form a triangle with two teammates, and always give the passer a clear line.

facts.text: Giráldez became Barcelona Femení head coach in July 2021. His team won 10 of the 12 trophies available to them, including the Champions League in 2023 and 2024.
Before becoming head coach he worked as an assistant at Barcelona Femení. Later he coached the Washington Spirit in the United States and won the 2025 NWSL Challenge Cup.

Luis de la Fuente.why: Luis de la Fuente was a left-back who won La Liga with Athletic Bilbao. As a coach he spent years with Spain's youth teams, so he knew many of his players from when they were young. His Spain teams keep the ball well, press together and mix experienced players with brave young talent. Kids can learn from his trust in youth; when a coach gives you a chance, play with courage.

learn.text: De la Fuente's Spain have quick, skilful players who keep the ball in tight spaces. Practise in a busy square: dribble with small touches, keep your head up and find gaps between the other players.

facts.text: As a left-back with Athletic Bilbao he won two La Liga titles, including a league and Copa del Rey double in 1984.
He won the European Under-19 and Under-21 Championships as a Spain youth coach. With the senior team he won the 2023 Nations League, Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup.

Dídac Plana.why: Dídac Plana is a Spanish futsal goalkeeper who has spent years guarding the goal for FC Barcelona. In futsal the goal is small and shots come from very close, so a keeper needs lightning reactions and brave, wide blocks. Dídac is also calm with the ball and starts attacks with quick throws and passes. Kids can learn from him that a goalkeeper is part of the team's attack as well as its last line of defence.

learn.text: Futsal shots arrive in a flash, so Dídac is always set before the strike. Practise taking small shuffling steps as the ball moves, then stop with your feet apart and your weight forward just before the shot.

facts.text: With FC Barcelona, Dídac won the UEFA Futsal Champions League in 2020 and 2022, as well as several Spanish league titles.
He was named the best male futsal goalkeeper in the world at the 2022 Futsal Awards, and he won the 2026 UEFA Futsal Euro with Spain.

Willian Dorn.why: Willian Dorn is a Brazilian futsal goalkeeper who became a hero at Joinville after joining the club as a teenager. He is quick off his line, brave in one-on-ones and good at starting attacks with fast throws. In futsal, a keeper who reads the game well can stop a chance before it even becomes a shot. Kids can copy his bravery; stay big, stay on your feet as long as you can, and make the attacker decide first.

learn.text: Dorn closes down attackers to make the goal look small. Practise narrowing the angle: step out along the line between the ball and the middle of the goal, stay big and stay balanced as the attacker gets close.

facts.text: Dorn spent eleven seasons with Joinville in Brazil and won the national league with them in 2017. In 2023 Futsal Planet voted him the best futsal goalkeeper in the world.
He won the 2024 FIFA Futsal World Cup with Brazil and was given the Golden Glove as the best goalkeeper of the tournament.

Guitta.why: Guitta is a Brazilian futsal goalkeeper famous for his explosive reflexes and his saves in one-on-one moments. Futsal keepers face shots from very close range, so they need to react in a split second and spread themselves wide. Guitta is also confident with the ball and helps his team build attacks. Kids can learn from his focus; keep your eyes on the ball all the way, even when the play is fast.

learn.text: Good keepers like Guitta hold on to the ball when they can. Practise catching with your hands in a W shape for high shots and a basket shape for low ones, then pull the ball safely into your chest.

facts.text: Guitta has won the FIFA Futsal World Cup twice with Brazil, in 2012 and 2024.
His real name is Thiago Mendes Rocha. In 2021 Futsal Planet named him the best futsal goalkeeper in the world.

Higuita.why: Leo Higuita is a goalkeeper who plays almost like an outfield player. Born in Brazil, he plays for Kazakhstan and is famous for dribbling out of his area, passing like a midfielder and even scoring goals. In futsal a keeper who can join the attack gives the team an extra player. Kids can learn from him that goalkeepers should practise with their feet too, so they are useful all over the pitch.

learn.text: Higuita starts attacks with his feet and his throws. Practise distribution: after a save, look up quickly, then roll or throw the ball accurately into the path of a teammate who is already running into space.

facts.text: His real name is Leonardo de Melo Vieira Leite. Because he scores goals, he was nicknamed after the famous Colombian goalkeeper René Higuita.
Higuita has played for the Kazakh club Kairat since 2011 and won the UEFA Futsal Champions League in 2013 and 2015.

Luis Amado.why: Luis Amado is one of Spain's greatest futsal goalkeepers. He played for his country well over a hundred times and spent many years at Inter Movistar near Madrid. He was known for his calm, his positioning and his quick saves in tight spaces. Being in the right spot means a keeper does not always need a diving save. Kids can learn from his positioning; think about where to stand before the shot comes.

learn.text: Amado was famous for standing in the right place. Practise your starting position: as the ball moves, take small steps so you are always on the line between the ball and the centre of your goal.

facts.text: Luis Amado won the FIFA Futsal World Cup with Spain twice, in 2000 in Guatemala and in 2004 in Chinese Taipei. He played 135 times for his country.
With Inter Movistar he won three UEFA Futsal Cups and six Spanish league titles.

Stefano Mammarella.why: Stefano Mammarella is an Italian futsal goalkeeper known for his quick reflexes and leadership. He organises the players in front of him and is brave when attackers get close. In futsal the keeper also has to start attacks quickly, and Mammarella is good at spotting a teammate in space. Kids can learn from his leadership; talk to your defenders and tell them where to stand.

learn.text: A keeper like Mammarella makes sure there is no rebound to tap in. Practise getting your body behind the ball and catching it cleanly, so shots stop dead in your hands instead of bouncing back out.

facts.text: Mammarella won the 2014 UEFA Futsal Championship with Italy. He was also named best goalkeeper at the 2012 FIFA Futsal World Cup, where Italy won bronze.
At club level he won the UEFA Futsal Cup with Montesilvano in 2011 and Serie A titles with Montesilvano and Acqua e Sapone.

Paco Sedano.why: Paco Sedano was a Spanish futsal goalkeeper who played in a long career that ended at Barcelona. He was known for staying calm under pressure and making big saves in the most important games. He began at small clubs and worked his way up to the top. Kids can learn from his journey; keep training hard, and your chance at a bigger level can come later in your career.

learn.text: Sedano was always balanced when the shot came. Practise moving across your goal with quick side steps, then getting set with your knees bent and your hands ready, so you can push off to either side.

facts.text: Sedano won the 2004 FIFA Futsal World Cup with Spain and two European Championships, in 2005 and 2016.
With Barcelona he won the UEFA Futsal Cup in 2011 and three Spanish league titles in a row.

Mostafa Nazari.why: Mostafa Nazari is an Iranian goalkeeper who helped make Iran one of the strongest futsal nations in Asia. He was known for his reflexes, his bravery and his quick throws that launched attacks. After his playing days he became a futsal coach. Kids can learn from his quick thinking; the moment you catch the ball, look up, because a fast throw can start a goal at the other end.

learn.text: Nazari's throws turned defence into attack. Practise a fast, flat overarm throw to a teammate running forward, aiming in front of them so they can take it in their stride.

facts.text: Nazari was chosen as the best futsal goalkeeper in the world in 2010.
He won the AFC Futsal Championship three times with Iran, and the Asian club championship with three different clubs.

Sergey Zuev.why: Sergey Zuev is a Russian futsal goalkeeper who was one of the best in the world in his prime. He was famous for amazing reflexes, quick feet and saves that seemed impossible. He started playing in his home town and worked his way up to the national team. Kids can learn from his reactions; keep your weight on the front of your feet, so you can spring in any direction.

learn.text: Zuev gave attackers very little to aim at. Practise coming out to meet a dribbler, staying upright and wide, and making yourself big so the attacker has to shoot straight at you.

facts.text: Zuev was voted the best goalkeeper of the Russian futsal championship in eight different seasons, and he was named the world's best goalkeeper for 2008.
As a young player he won the Student World Cup with a Russian student team before making his debut for Russia's senior national team.

Tiago Marinho.why: Tiago Marinho, known simply as Tiago, is a Brazilian futsal goalkeeper who was part of two World Cup-winning teams. He was known for his agility, his quick saves and his calm in big games. A futsal keeper has to react to shots from very close, often with a foot or a quick hand. Kids can learn from his agility; practise moving quickly in all directions, not just diving.

learn.text: Tiago made sure the ball stayed in his hands. Practise with a partner throwing at you from close range, catching each ball and holding it against your chest before throwing it back.

facts.text: Tiago won the FIFA Futsal World Cup with Brazil in 2008 and again in 2012.
In 2007 he was named the best futsal goalkeeper of the year by Futsal Planet.

Antonio Pérez.why: Antonio Pérez is a Spanish futsal defender who plays as a fixo, the player at the back who organises the team and starts attacks. He is strong in duels, reads passes early and is also dangerous with long-range shots. In futsal the fixo often has to be the last defender and the first attacker at the same time. Kids can learn from him that defenders who can pass and shoot help the whole team.

learn.text: Antonio is calm when an attacker runs at him. Practise jockeying in a small space: stay side-on, keep a short distance, watch the ball and only step in when the attacker takes a heavy touch.

facts.text: Antonio won the UEFA Under-19 Futsal Championship with Spain in 2019. With the senior team he won the 2026 UEFA Futsal Euro and was named Player of the Tournament.
At the 2026 Futsal Euro he also won the Golden Boot as the top scorer.

Tomás Paçó.why: Tomás Paçó is a Portuguese futsal defender known for his strength, his timing in tackles and his calm passing from the back. He came through at Sporting CP and has become a key player for club and country. A good fixo talks to teammates, covers spaces and makes sure the team never gets caught out. Kids can copy his concentration; keep watching the ball and your opponent, even when play is at the other end.

learn.text: Tomás always gets back between the ball and his goal. Practise reacting when you lose the ball, sprinting back on the inside path towards your goal, and then turning to face the attacker before you tackle.

facts.text: Tomás Paçó has a twin brother, Bernardo, who is a professional futsal goalkeeper.
With Sporting CP he won the UEFA Futsal Champions League in 2021 and 2026. With Portugal he won the 2021 FIFA Futsal World Cup and the European Championship in 2022 and 2026.

André Coelho.why: André Coelho is a Portuguese futsal player described as a universal, which means he can defend, pass and attack equally well. He is known for his powerful shooting and his smart positioning. Universal players are very important in futsal because everybody has to attack and defend. Kids can learn from his all-round game; practise every skill, not just one, so you can help your team anywhere on the court.

learn.text: Coelho is famous for strong, accurate shots. Practise striking the ball with your laces, keeping your head over the ball and your non-kicking foot beside it, so the shot stays low and hard.

facts.text: Coelho won the FIFA Futsal World Cup with Portugal in 2021, plus the European Championship in 2018 and 2022.
He has also played for Barcelona, where he won the UEFA Futsal Champions League in 2022 and three Spanish league titles in a row.

Afonso Jesus.why: Afonso Jesus is a Portuguese futsal defender who has spent his career at Benfica. He is a calm organiser at the back, good at reading the game and starting attacks with clever passes. Futsal defenders need quick feet because the court is small and the ball moves fast. Kids can learn from his reading of the game; look at where the attacker wants to pass, and step into the passing line.

learn.text: Afonso and his partner defend as a pair. Practise covering: when your teammate presses the ball, stand a few steps behind them at an angle, ready to step in if the attacker gets past.

facts.text: Afonso Jesus won the 2021 FIFA Futsal World Cup, the 2022 European Championship and the 2022 Futsal Finalissima with Portugal.
He plays for Benfica, and with them he has won the Portuguese league four times, as of November 2026.

Kike Boned.why: Kike Boned was a Spanish futsal defender who was one of the best players in the world in his time. He was strong, smart and a natural leader at the back. He played in four World Cup finals for Spain, which shows how long he stayed at the top. Kids can learn from his consistency; good habits in every training session help you play well for many years.

learn.text: Kike won many one-on-one battles. Practise in a one-against-one game with two small goals: stay patient, block the shooting line with your body and win the ball when the attacker makes a mistake.

facts.text: Kike was named the 2009 Futsal Player of the Year by Futsal Planet.
He is one of only two players to have been part of four FIFA Futsal World Cup final teams, in 2000, 2004, 2008 and 2012. Spain won the first two.

Schumacher.why: Schumacher was a Brazilian futsal player whose real name is Flávio Sérgio Viana. He was strong, skilful and a leader on the court, and he could defend and attack with power. He played for big clubs in Brazil and Spain. Kids can learn from his toughness; in futsal every player has to defend, so be ready to win the ball back as soon as it is lost.

learn.text: Schumacher reacted quickly when his team lost the ball. Practise switching from attacker to defender fast, chasing the ball straight away and trying to win it back before the other team can settle.

facts.text: He was elected the best futsal player in the world for 2008.
His nickname comes from the German football goalkeeper Harald Schumacher, not the racing driver.

Gabriel.why: Gabriel was a Brazilian futsal star who won almost everything with Inter Movistar and Barcelona. He was quick, clever and able to play in different positions, defending well and joining attacks down the side. He played in many big finals and stayed calm in all of them. Kids can learn from his work rate; help your team at both ends of the court.

learn.text: Gabriel loved quick passing combinations down the side. Practise the one-two with a friend, passing and then sprinting forward right away so you can receive the return pass in space behind the defender.

facts.text: Gabriel won the UEFA Futsal Champions League four times and the FIFA Futsal World Cup twice, in 2008 and 2012.
He also won a gold medal in futsal with Brazil at the 2007 Pan American Games.

Carlos Ortiz.why: Carlos Ortiz, known as Ortiz, is a Spanish futsal defender and leader. He was famous for his timing in tackles, his positioning and his long career at the top. He often organised the team from the back, telling teammates where to go. Kids can learn from his leadership; a good defender talks all the time and helps teammates stay in the right place.

learn.text: Ortiz made sure his team defended together. Practise talking while you defend, calling who is pressing and who is covering, so you and your partner always know each other's jobs.

facts.text: Ortiz won the UEFA Futsal Championship with Spain in 2007 and played in the 2008 FIFA Futsal World Cup final.
He won the UEFA Futsal Champions League in 2009 and was picked as a defender in FutsalFeed's Best Team of the Year in 2020.

Aicardo.why: Aicardo is a Spanish futsal defender from Cádiz who became an important player for Barcelona. He is strong in tackles and calm when building attacks. As the fixo he often stays behind the ball, protecting the team against counter-attacks. Kids can learn from his awareness; when your team attacks, someone needs to stay back, and that job is just as important.

learn.text: Aicardo is the safety net when his team attacks. Practise staying behind the ball while your teammates go forward, and sprint back towards your goal the moment the other team wins possession.

facts.text: Aicardo won the UEFA Futsal Champions League in the 2019-20 season, a year after finishing third in the same competition.
His full name is Jesús Nazaret Aicardo Collantes, and he has played for the Spain national futsal team.

Neto.why: Neto is a Brazilian futsal defender known for his calm, his strength and his ability to score important goals. A fixo has to defend well, but the best ones also pass forward and shoot from distance. Neto did all of that and became one of the leaders of the Brazil team. Kids can learn from his composure; in a big moment, stay calm and do the simple thing well.

learn.text: Neto could arrive late and shoot from distance. Practise playing a pass into a teammate, running onto their lay-off, and striking it first time towards the corner of the goal.

facts.text: Neto won the 2012 FIFA Futsal World Cup with Brazil and was given the Golden Ball as the best player of the tournament.
He won the 2011 futsal Copa América with Brazil and was named the best player of that tournament.

Julio García Mera.why: Julio García Mera was a Spanish futsal defender best known for many years at Inter Movistar. He was a reliable, intelligent player who helped Spain become one of the strongest futsal nations. He was strong in tackles and good at starting moves from the back. Kids can learn from his reliability; a defender the team can always trust is worth a lot.

learn.text: García Mera rarely let attackers get past. Practise defending in a one-against-one game with end zones: stay on your toes, keep the attacker in front of you and force them away from the middle.

facts.text: García Mera won the FIFA Futsal World Cup with Spain in Guatemala in 2000, after finishing runner-up at the 1996 World Cup in Spain.
With Inter Movistar he won five Spanish league titles and the UEFA Futsal Cup in 2004.

Marcio Forte.why: Márcio Forte is a Brazilian-born futsal defender who became a leader for Italy's national team. He played for many years in Italy, including spells with Lazio. A fixo like Forte protects the team at the back, wins tackles and starts attacks with clever passes. Kids can learn from his leadership and reliability; be the player your team can count on in defence, and then help start the attack.

learn.text: Forte helped his team play out from the back. Practise receiving from your keeper, turning away from pressure and passing firmly to a teammate who is moving into space further up the court.

facts.text: Márcio Forte was born in Londrina in Brazil and moved to Italy, where he went on to play for the Italian national futsal team and the club Lazio.

Douglas Junior.why: Douglas Júnior is a Brazilian-born futsal player who became an international for Kazakhstan. He is known for his powerful shooting and his strength on the ball. Players who can shoot hard from distance are dangerous in futsal, because even a deflection can beat the goalkeeper. Kids can learn from his shooting; practise striking the ball cleanly, and keep shots low and on target.

learn.text: Douglas is dangerous whenever he has space to shoot. Practise dribbling forward a few touches, setting the ball slightly in front of you, and striking it hard and low towards the corner.

facts.text: Born in Brazil, Douglas Júnior went on to play for the Kazakhstan national team. He also reached the UEFA Futsal Champions League final in 2019.

Ricardinho.why: Ricardinho, nicknamed "O Mágico", which means The Magician, is a Portuguese futsal winger and one of the most skilful players the sport has ever seen. He is famous for tricks, flicks and dribbles that leave defenders spinning, but also for clever passes that set up teammates. He usually wears number 10. Kids can learn from his creativity; practise tricks with both feet, then use them to beat a defender and make a goal.

learn.text: Ricardinho keeps the ball glued to his feet. Practise weaving through cones using the sole, inside and outside of both feet, keeping the ball very close so you can change direction in a flash.

facts.text: Futsal Planet named Ricardinho the Best Player of the World a record six times, including five years in a row from 2014 to 2018.
He helped Portugal win the 2018 UEFA Futsal Euro and the 2021 FIFA Futsal World Cup. He also won the UEFA Futsal Cup with Benfica and with Inter Movistar.

Falcão.why: Falcão is a Brazilian futsal legend, often called the greatest futsal player of all time. He was famous for flashy dribbling, clever skills and a powerful, accurate left foot. Defenders never knew which trick he would use next. After retiring he started teaching futsal skills to young players around the world. Kids can learn from his joy and imagination; try new tricks in training, and do not be afraid to make mistakes.

learn.text: Falcão loved to take on defenders. Practise one-against-one dribbling: run at the defender, use a feint or a step-over to make them lean one way, then go quickly the other way.

facts.text: Falcão was named the Best Futsal Player in the World four times and won the FIFA Futsal World Cup Golden Ball in 2004 and 2008.
In 2005 he briefly played 11-a-side football for São Paulo, including in that year's Copa Libertadores, before going back to futsal.

Manoel Tobias.why: Manoel Tobias was a Brazilian futsal star of the 1990s, known for his speed, his skill and his eye for goal. He played for many teams across Brazil and won titles wherever he went. He helped make Brazil the team everyone wanted to beat. Kids can learn from his quick feet and quick thinking; in futsal, a fast decision is often more important than a fancy trick.

learn.text: Tobias could change direction in a moment. Practise dribbling at speed, stopping the ball with your sole, and turning sharply to accelerate away the other way.

facts.text: Manoel Tobias won the FIFA Futsal World Cup with Brazil twice, in 1992 and 1996.
He also won the South American Club Futsal Championship in 1993 and the Intercontinental Futsal Cup in 1996 and 1998.

Javi Rodríguez.why: Javi Rodríguez is a Spanish futsal winger who is considered one of the greatest players in the history of the sport. He was quick, clever and a natural goalscorer, and he stayed at the top for many years. He played in four World Cup finals for Spain. Kids can learn from his long career; look after your body, keep practising and keep loving the game.

learn.text: Javi knew when to pass and when to shoot. Practise two against one: dribble at the defender, and if they come to you, pass to your free teammate, but if they stay back, shoot.

facts.text: Futsal Planet named Javi Rodríguez the 2005 Futsal Player of the Year.
He played in four FIFA Futsal World Cup finals, in 1996, 2000, 2004 and 2008, and won the trophy with Spain in 2000 and 2004.

Sergio Lozano.why: Sergio Lozano is a Spanish futsal winger known for his powerful shot and his clever movement. He has spent many years at Barcelona and helped them win big trophies at home and in Europe. A good ala moves into space at the right moment and is always ready to shoot. Kids can learn from his timing; run into space just as your teammate is ready to pass.

learn.text: Lozano scores lots of goals with first-time shots. Practise receiving a pass across your body and striking it first time, keeping your knee over the ball so the shot stays low.

facts.text: Lozano has won the UEFA Futsal Cup four times and won the 2012 UEFA Futsal Euro with Spain.
In 2020 he was picked as a winger in FutsalFeed's Best Team of the Year.

Daniel Ibañes.why: Daniel Ibañes is a Brazilian-born futsal player who became a star for Spain and Inter Movistar. He was an ala, quick and skilful down the sides, and very good at creating chances for teammates. He was part of the great Inter team that won titles year after year. Kids can learn from his teamwork; a winger who passes at the right time makes the whole team dangerous.

learn.text: Ibañes set up goals from the wing. Practise dribbling down the side, looking up, and passing the ball low across the goal for a teammate arriving at the far post.

facts.text: Ibañes won the 2000 FIFA Futsal World Cup with Spain and four European Championships.
With Inter Movistar he won five Spanish league titles and three UEFA Futsal Cups.

Robinho.why: Robinho is a Brazilian-born futsal winger who became an international for Russia. He is quick, tricky and dangerous in one-on-one situations, and he has played in Belgium, Russia and Portugal. In futsal an ala who can beat a defender creates space for everyone else. Kids can learn from his bravery; when you get the ball on the wing, be confident and take your defender on.

learn.text: Robinho likes to attack defenders one-on-one. Practise in a one-against-one game with two small goals, faking to go one way and then accelerating past the defender the other way.

facts.text: Robinho won the UEFA Futsal Cup twice, with Action 21 Charleroi in 2005 and with Gazprom-Ugra Yugorsk in 2016.
Playing for Russia, he reached the final of the 2016 FIFA Futsal World Cup, where Russia were runners-up.

Alex Merlim.why: Alex Merlim, also known as Babalu, is a Brazilian-born futsal winger who plays for Italy. He has spent many years at Sporting CP in Portugal, where he became one of the team's leaders. He is clever with the ball, works hard for the team and has a good shot. Kids can learn from his work rate; a winger who also helps in defence is a great teammate.

learn.text: Merlim loves quick combinations with his teammates. Practise a wall pass by playing the ball into a teammate, sprinting forward straight away, and taking the return pass as you run into space.

facts.text: Alex Merlim, also called Babalu, was born in Brazil and plays international futsal for Italy.
With Sporting CP he has won the UEFA Futsal Champions League three times, in 2019, 2021 and 2026.

Miguelín.why: Miguelín is a Spanish futsal winger from Palma in Majorca, best known for his time at ElPozo Murcia. He is a skilful ala who likes to dribble, combine with teammates and shoot from the wing. In futsal the alas run up and down the sides, helping in both attack and defence. Kids can learn from his energy; keep moving, offer passes and get back when your team loses the ball.

learn.text: Miguelín likes to keep the ball close as he dribbles. Practise dribbling through lots of small gates, looking up after each one to find the next gate before another player gets there.

facts.text: Miguelín's full name is Miguel Sayago Martí. He is a Spanish futsal player who has played as an ala for ElPozo Murcia.

Jordi Torras.why: Jordi Torras is a Spanish futsal player who could play on the wing or at the back, which made him very useful to his coaches. He was a hard-working, intelligent player who rarely made mistakes. He won many trophies, including with Inter Movistar. Kids can learn from his versatility; being able to play in more than one position helps you get on the court.

learn.text: Torras could defend as well as attack. Practise with a partner taking turns pressing the ball and covering, so you learn both jobs and can switch whenever the play changes.

facts.text: Torras won the 2004 FIFA Futsal World Cup with Spain and four UEFA Futsal Championships.
At club level he won the UEFA Futsal Cup three times, in 2009, 2012 and 2014.

Zicky Té.why: Zicky Té is a Portuguese futsal pivot, born in Guinea-Bissau, who came through at Sporting CP. The pivot plays furthest forward, often with their back to goal, holding the ball up so teammates can join the attack. Zicky is strong, quick to turn and calm in front of goal. Kids can learn from his hold-up play; protect the ball with your body, wait for support, then pass or turn and shoot.

learn.text: Zicky is great at receiving with his back to goal. Practise shielding the ball from a partner, feeling where they are, then turning quickly the other way to face the goal.

facts.text: Zicky Té was born in Guinea-Bissau and plays international futsal for Portugal. He won the 2021 FIFA Futsal World Cup and the 2022 European Championship with them.
He was part of the Sporting CP team that won the UEFA Futsal Champions League in 2021 and 2026.

Pito.why: Pito is a Brazilian futsal player who can play as a pivot or on the wing. He is strong, skilful and clever at finding space near the goal. He has played for top clubs in Brazil and Spain and won trophies with all of them. Kids can learn from his movement; in a small space, a quick step away from your defender is often all you need to get free for a shot.

learn.text: Pito always knows where the defender is. Practise checking over your shoulder before the ball arrives, so you know whether to turn or lay the ball off to a teammate.

facts.text: Pito won the 2024 FIFA Futsal World Cup with Brazil.
Before moving to Spain he won Brazil's national futsal league with Carlos Barbosa in 2015. In Spain he has won league titles with Inter and Barcelona.

Jesús Gordillo.why: Jesús Gordillo is a Spanish futsal pivot known for his strength, his movement and his finishing. As a young player he was part of Spain's youth teams before breaking into the senior side. A good pivot keeps defenders busy and creates space for everyone else. Kids can learn from his work without the ball; keep moving, pull defenders around and be ready when the pass comes.

learn.text: Pivots like Gordillo score lots of goals from rebounds. Practise following every shot towards the goal, so if the keeper spills the ball you are there first to tap it in.

facts.text: With Palma Futsal, Gordillo won the UEFA Futsal Champions League three seasons in a row, from 2022-23 to 2024-25.
He won the UEFA Under-19 Futsal Championship with Spain in 2019 and the senior UEFA Futsal Euro with Spain in 2026.

Higor.why: Higor is a Brazilian futsal pivot known for strong back-to-goal turns and quick finishes in the box. A pivot has to hold off defenders, keep the ball and then either shoot or bring teammates into the game. Higor came through in Brazil before moving to clubs in Europe. Kids can learn from his strength on the ball; use your body to protect the ball, and keep it close.

learn.text: A pivot like Higor has to control passes that come at all heights. Practise cushioning the ball with your thigh and your chest, so it drops right at your feet, ready to play.

facts.text: Higor Ribeiro de Souza started his career at Corinthians in Brazil, winning the Copa do Brasil de Futsal in 2019. He has played for the Brazil national futsal team.

Ferrão.why: Ferrão is a Brazilian futsal pivot and one of the best of his generation. He is strong, powerful and very hard to push off the ball, and he scores many goals from close range. He spent years at Barcelona, where he won big trophies. Kids can learn from his determination; keep fighting for the ball near goal, because many goals come from second chances.

learn.text: Ferrão often holds the ball and sets up teammates. Practise receiving a pass with your back to goal, laying it off to a running teammate with one touch, and then spinning to look for the return.

facts.text: Ferrão was voted the world's best futsal player three years in a row, in 2019, 2020 and 2021.
He won the UEFA Futsal Champions League twice and, in 2024, the FIFA Futsal World Cup with Brazil.

Vander Carioca.why: Vander Carioca was a Brazilian futsal forward who played for a long time in Brazil and Spain. He was known for his finishing, his clever movement and his experience. He kept playing at a high level for many years and won titles at several clubs. Kids can learn from his love of the game; if you enjoy training and keep learning, you can keep improving for a long time.

learn.text: Vander was a sharp finisher. Practise dribbling a few touches towards goal and then shooting quickly, before the defender can close you down, aiming low for the corners.

facts.text: His real name is Vander dos Santos Ferreira. He won the Copa América de Futsal with Brazil in 1998 and 1999.
He won Brazil's national futsal league with Vasco da Gama in 2000 and again with Corinthians in 2016.

Wilde.why: Wilde is a Brazilian futsal pivot who was a key player for Barcelona and Brazil. He was strong, good at holding the ball and dangerous in front of goal. A pivot like Wilde gives the team a target to pass to, which helps the whole team push forward. Kids can learn from his patience; wait for the right moment, then strike.

learn.text: Wilde could receive and play in one move. Practise receiving a pass across your body with your back foot, opening up so you can see the goal and play forward straight away.

facts.text: Wilde won the FIFA Futsal World Cup twice with Brazil, in 2008 and 2012.
He won the UEFA Futsal Cup twice and seven Spanish league titles.

Lenísio.why: Lenísio was a Brazilian futsal pivot and one of the top scorers of his time in Brazil and Spain. He was strong, clever and lethal near goal. He won many awards as the best player and best pivot. Kids can learn from his finishing; practise shooting with both feet so you can score whichever way the ball comes to you.

learn.text: Lenísio scored from all kinds of positions. Practise shooting with your weaker foot as well as your stronger one, so defenders cannot stop you by blocking one side.

facts.text: Lenísio won the 2008 FIFA Futsal World Cup with Brazil, after reaching the final in 2000.
In Spain he was named the best player of the LNFS league three seasons in a row and was its top scorer twice.

Konstantin Eremenko.why: Konstantin Eremenko was a Russian futsal player and a true legend of the sport. He was a brilliant goalscorer, clever with the ball and a leader for his club and country. He helped make Russia one of the strongest teams in Europe. Kids can learn from his greatness in a simple way; he practised his skills again and again until they were perfect.

learn.text: Great players like Eremenko master the basics first. Practise toe taps, sole rolls and inside-outside touches every day, keeping the ball close and your head up as you get quicker.

facts.text: Konstantin Eremenko, also spelled Yeryomenko, was named the greatest futsal player of the 20th century.
He won the Russian Futsal Super League eight times in a row and the European club title three times. With Russia he won the 1999 UEFA Futsal Championship.

Eder Lima.why: Éder Lima is a Brazilian-born futsal pivot who plays for Russia. He is strong, tall and a fantastic finisher, scoring many goals at big tournaments. A pivot like Éder gives the team a powerful target near the goal. Kids can learn from his finishing; when you get a chance near goal, stay calm and hit the target.

learn.text: Éder is always in the right place for goals. Practise moving into the space in front of the goal after a teammate shoots, ready to finish any rebound before the defenders react.

facts.text: Éder Lima won the Golden Shoe as top scorer at the 2012 FIFA Futsal World Cup and at the 2014 UEFA Futsal Euro.
Born in Brazil, he went on to represent Russia, and he won the Silver Shoe at the 2016 FIFA Futsal World Cup.

Cirilo.why: Cirilo is a Brazilian-born futsal player who became an international for Russia. He spent many successful years in Russian futsal, winning title after title. He was known for his power, his finishing and his experience. Kids can learn from his consistency; a player who performs well every week helps the team win championships.

learn.text: Even forwards like Cirilo have to defend in futsal. Practise pressing a player who has the ball, staying on your feet, showing them away from goal and staying close.

facts.text: Cirilo won the Russian Futsal Super League seven times and the UEFA Futsal Cup in 2007.
Born in Brazil, he played for the Russian national futsal team, finishing third at the 2007 UEFA Futsal Championship.

Joel Queirós.why: Joel Queirós is a Portuguese futsal pivot known for his goalscoring and his strength in front of goal. He played in Portugal and Spain and won league titles in both countries. He was one of Portugal's top players for many years. Kids can learn from his determination near goal; keep making runs into the box, even if the ball does not come every time.

learn.text: Joel attacked the space in front of goal. Practise timing your run so you arrive just as the ball comes across, and finish first time with the inside of your foot.

facts.text: Joel Queirós won the Golden Boot as top scorer at the 2010 UEFA Futsal Championship, where Portugal finished runners-up.
He won the UEFA Futsal Cup with Benfica in 2010, and Spanish league titles with ElPozo Murcia.

Fernandão.why: Fernandão is a Brazilian-born futsal pivot who played for Spain. He was famous for his strength and his finishing, and he was very hard to move off the ball. He won many trophies with Barcelona. Kids can learn from his strength and positioning; get between the defender and the ball, so the pass can only reach you.

learn.text: Fernandão protected the ball with his body. Practise receiving with your back to a defender, keeping the ball on your far foot, and turning away from the side where the defender is pressing.

facts.text: Born in Brazil, Fernandão played for the Spain national futsal team and reached the 2008 FIFA Futsal World Cup final.
He won the UEFA Futsal Cup twice, in 2012 and 2014, and three Spanish league titles.

Cardinal.why: Fernando Cardinal is a Portuguese futsal pivot known for his strength, his hold-up play and his finishing. He became an important player for Sporting CP and Portugal. A pivot like Cardinal fights for every ball near goal and brings teammates into the attack. Kids can learn from his work rate; as the furthest player forward, you are the first defender too.

learn.text: Cardinal links up play with quick one-twos. Practise passing into a teammate, then spinning away from your defender and running into space to receive the return pass near goal.

facts.text: Fernando Cardinal won the UEFA Futsal Champions League in the 2018-19 season and has played for the Portugal national futsal team.

Bernardo Paçó.why: Bernardo Paçó is a Portuguese futsal goalkeeper who grew up in Sporting CP's academy and became the team's keeper. He is quick, brave and good with his feet, so he can help his team keep the ball. In futsal the goalkeeper is often the first attacker, starting moves with a throw or a pass. Kids can learn from him that goalkeepers should practise passing and throwing as much as saving.

learn.text: Bernardo starts attacks quickly after a save. Practise rolling the ball out fast and accurately to a teammate's feet, then try throwing it further to a teammate who is running into space.

facts.text: Bernardo Paçó has a twin brother, Tomás, who plays futsal as a defender for Sporting CP and Portugal.
With Sporting CP he won the Portuguese futsal league four seasons in a row, from 2020-21 to 2023-24.

Santiago Elías.why: Santiago Elías is an Argentine futsal goalkeeper who played for many years at the top level. He is known for his reflexes, his courage in one-on-ones and his calm voice organising the defence. Argentina became one of the strongest futsal nations while he was in goal. Kids can learn from his courage; stay big and brave when an attacker is through, and make yourself hard to beat.

learn.text: Santiago makes the goal look tiny for the shooter. Practise stepping forward towards the ball, staying on your feet with your arms wide, so the attacker has very little space to aim at.

facts.text: Santiago Elías won the Argentine futsal league many times with the club Pinocho. He was also named the best goalkeeper at the Futsal Awards for 2009.

Ricardo Mayor.why: Ricardo Mayor is a Spanish futsal defender who came through the youth teams in Murcia. He plays as the last defender, so he reads danger early, wins tackles and starts attacks with calm passes. Spain have a long history of strong futsal defenders, and Mayor is part of the new generation. Kids can learn from his calm defending; stay patient, and wait for the right moment to win the ball.

learn.text: Mayor rarely dives in. Practise defending in a one-against-one game with two small goals, keeping your feet moving and waiting for the attacker to make a mistake before you step in.

facts.text: Ricardo Mayor won the UEFA Under-19 Futsal Championship with Spain in 2022, then the senior UEFA Futsal Euro with Spain in 2026.

Adrián Rivera.why: Adrián Rivera is a young Spanish futsal player who has already won European titles with Spain at youth and senior level. He can defend and attack, and he is confident with the ball. In futsal every player needs to be able to do both jobs. Kids can learn from his confidence; when you get a chance to shoot, take it.

learn.text: Rivera is not afraid to shoot. Practise dribbling forward with your head up, picking your spot early, and finishing with a firm, low shot before a defender can block it.

facts.text: Adrián Rivera won the UEFA Under-19 Futsal Championship with Spain in 2022 and the senior UEFA Futsal Euro in 2026.
He won Spain's second division twice, with Noia in 2021 and with S10 Zaragoza in 2024.

Catela.why: Catela is a Spanish futsal winger who has won big trophies with FC Barcelona. He is quick, skilful and good at combining with teammates down the sides, often with short one-two passes. In futsal the alas must attack and then sprint back to defend. Kids can learn from his effort; after every attack, get back into position so your team is never caught out.

learn.text: Catela keeps the ball under control in crowded spaces. Practise dribbling in a busy square, using small touches and quick changes of direction to find the open spaces.

facts.text: With Barcelona, Catela won the Spanish futsal league in 2022-23 and 2025-26 and the Copa del Rey in 2022-23.

Luciano Gauna.why: Luciano Gauna is an Argentine futsal winger who shone at Peñíscola in Spain before joining Barcelona. He is quick, clever with the ball and good at finding teammates. Argentina have become one of the best futsal teams in the world, with skilful players like him. Kids can learn from his vision; look up while you dribble so you can spot the pass that splits the defence.

learn.text: Gauna knows when to dribble and when to pass. Practise two against one, drawing the defender towards you before slipping the ball to your free teammate.

facts.text: Gauna won the Copa de España with Peñíscola in 2025, and the Spanish futsal league with Barcelona in 2025-26.

Raúl Gómez.why: Raúl Gómez is a Spanish futsal pivot who has also played in Russia. He is strong with his back to goal, holds the ball well and brings his teammates into the attack. A good pivot is the target for long passes and the first defender when the team loses the ball. Kids can learn from his hold-up play; protect the ball, wait for support and then pass.

learn.text: A pivot like Raúl has to control passes at any height. Practise cushioning a thrown ball with your thigh or chest, so it drops close to your feet and you can keep it under pressure.

facts.text: Before returning to Spain, Raúl Gómez won the Russian futsal league with KPRF Moscow in the 2019-20 season.

Souheil Mouhoudine.why: Souheil Mouhoudine is a French futsal player who studied sport at university while building his career. He is quick, clever and dangerous near goal, and he loves to take on defenders in one-on-one situations. Kids can learn from his journey; he started at local clubs and kept improving until he played at the highest level.

learn.text: Mouhoudine loves to run at defenders. Practise one-against-one with end zones, using a quick feint and a burst of speed to get past your defender and reach the zone.

facts.text: In 2018 Mouhoudine played for the French university futsal team that finished fourth at the world championships in Brazil, and he was voted best player of the tournament.
He won the French futsal championship with ASC Garges Djibson in the 2016-17 season.

Sid Belhaj.why: Sid Belhaj is a French futsal defender and a leader for club and country. He organises the team from the back, wins the ball with good timing and starts attacks with calm passes. He has won the French title with more than one club, which shows how much coaches trust him. Kids can learn from his leadership; talk to your teammates and help them stay organised.

learn.text: Belhaj helps his team play out from the back. Practise receiving from the goalkeeper on the half-turn, then passing forward into a teammate who has moved into space.

facts.text: Sid Belhaj has won the French futsal championship four times, in 2015, 2016, 2021 and 2022, and the Coupe de France twice.

Ouassini Guirio.why: Ouassini Guirio is a French futsal international known for his finishing and his big-game goals. He has won trophies with clubs in different parts of France. He is quick, sharp and always looking to get on the end of chances. Kids can learn from his never-give-up attitude; one big moment can change a whole game.

learn.text: Guirio is always ready for a second chance. Practise following up every shot towards the goal so you are first to any rebound the keeper cannot hold.
